text: Grip a little wider than shoulders, sit tall.

review.notes: Andersen found similar lat activity across grip widths, medium slightly stronger; the 'sit tall' part is convention.

text: Pull the bar to your collarbone, not behind your neck.

review.notes: Supported: Sperandei's authors prefer the front pulldown and advise avoiding behind-the-neck. Wording is ours.

text: Lean back only slightly; don't swing the weight.

review.notes: Convention. The source does not test torso lean or momentum.

text: Let the bar rise slowly, shoulders staying down.

review.notes: Andersen reports lat activity in the lowering phase; the shoulders-down cue is convention.

text: Hand and knee on bench, back flat.

review.notes: Convention. Fenwick studied standing rows, not a bench-supported row.

text: Pull your elbow toward your hip.

review.notes: Convention; Fenwick shows rows load the back muscles but does not test elbow path.

text: Shoulder blade back and down; don't twist your torso.

review.notes: Partly supported: Fenwick found the one-arm cable row makes the trunk muscles resist twisting. Blade cue is convention.

text: Lower slowly until your arm is straight.

review.notes: Convention.

text: Sit tall, legs out, band around your feet.

review.notes: Convention. OpenStax only supports that the rhomboids pull the shoulder blade back; no band-row study cited.

text: Pull your elbows back, trunk staying tall.

review.notes: Convention; anatomy source supports the shoulder-blade retraction idea only.

text: Squeeze shoulder blades together, shoulders away from ears.

review.notes: Convention; retraction action is from OpenStax, the shrug warning is ours.

text: Let the band return slowly, no slumping.

review.notes: Convention.

text: Hands on a sturdy bench, body in one line.

review.notes: Ebben supports that raising the hands lowers the push-up load; 'body in one line' is convention.

text: Look just ahead of your hands, neck long.

review.notes: Convention; no source on head position.

text: Lower your chest to the edge, elbows angled back.

review.notes: Convention; elbow angle is not tested in Ebben.

text: Press up, keeping hips level with shoulders.

review.notes: Convention.

text: Hands directly under your chest, fingers forward.

review.notes: Cogley found narrow hands gave more chest and triceps activity than wide; exact hand placement is convention.

text: Elbows brush your ribs on the way down.

review.notes: Convention; elbow path is not tested.

text: Press to full lockout, hips staying level.

review.notes: Convention.

text: Body in one straight line, neck long.

review.notes: Convention.

text: Elbows beside your ribs, palms forward.

review.notes: Oliveira shows shoulder position changes biceps activity; elbows-at-sides is convention.

text: Curl up without swinging your body.

review.notes: Convention; Marcolin measured strict curls only.

text: Pause briefly, shoulders down and still.

review.notes: Convention.

text: Lower slowly, elbow soft at the bottom.

review.notes: Oliveira found less biceps activity lowering than lifting; slow lowering is convention for control and elbow comfort.

text: Thumbs up, palms facing each other.

review.notes: OpenStax says the brachioradialis works most with thumb up, which matches a hammer grip. Not a hammer-curl study.

text: Curl up, keeping your elbows still.

review.notes: Convention. Marcolin tested no hammer grip.

text: Lower slowly, don't let the weight drop.

review.notes: Convention.

text: Body straight like a plank, heels on floor.

review.notes: Fenwick found the inverted row gave the lowest lumbar load of the rows tested; that presumes a straight body. Wording is ours.

text: Pull your chest to the bar, shoulder blades back.

review.notes: Youdas 2020 measured scapular muscle activity during the row in healthy people; cue wording is convention.

text: Keep your hips up all the way.

review.notes: Convention.

text: Lower slowly, body staying straight.

review.notes: Convention.

text: Start hanging, shoulders down away from your ears.

review.notes: Youdas reports lower trapezius activity in the pull-up; 'shoulders down' is convention.

text: Pull your chest toward the bar.

review.notes: Youdas measured lats, biceps and others in pull-ups; wording is ours.

text: Lower slowly; keep your shoulders active at the bottom.

review.notes: Convention, not tested. An injury-caution cue; worth a clinician's view.

text: Ribs down, glutes tight, no leaning back.

review.notes: Saeterbakken shows body position changes deltoid activity; the rib cue is convention.

text: Press straight up over your shoulders.

review.notes: Convention.

text: Lower to ear level, forearms upright.

review.notes: Convention.

text: Don't shrug; keep your neck relaxed.

review.notes: Convention; Saeterbakken measured deltoid, biceps and triceps, not the upper trapezius.
